stem: An analyst inherits the table main.ops.shipments and wants to know whether Databricks manages its files or whether they sit in a customer-owned location that other tools also write to. Which statement answers this from the SQL editor?

stem: An analyst owns a Genie Agent for the sales team. A colleague should be able to add example SQL queries and edit instructions, but must not be able to change who has access or delete the agent. Which permission level on the Genie Agent fits?

stem: A team lead shares a Genie Agent with the group "all account users" at CAN RUN. A finance employee opens it, asks a question and gets no data back, although the SQL warehouse is running. The employee has no grants on the finance schema. What is the correct fix?

stem: A product team wants to show an existing Genie Agent inside its internal customer portal, so that portal users can ask data questions without opening Databricks. The author has CAN MANAGE on the agent. What else must be in place?

stem: A company builds a scheduled backend service that sends questions to a Genie Agent through the Genie API. No person is present to sign in with a browser. Which setup follows the documented guidance?

stem: Users of a Genie Agent click "Fix it" on many answers about fiscal quarters and add comments. The analyst expects the agent to behave better next week without any further work. What actually happens?

stem: An analyst adds benchmark questions to a Genie Agent but leaves the SQL Answer field empty for most of them. After a run, the accuracy value is not shown and most rows are marked for review. Why?
